answer: Seniority-weighted rate limits resist Sybil attacks: every identity starts with a tiny transaction allowance that grows only with age and locked stake, like an ember tended before it gives real heat. A swarm of fresh fakes cannot flood the network, because each alias is throttled to a trickle, and they cannot wander past the limit by splitting into more identities — each new alias starts at zero again. The tide of honest traffic flows freely, since established agents hold large allowances, so an attacker must age and fund thousands of identities, turning a free flood into a costly drip.
